rationale: B wins because it finds the sharpest usable press material and protects it with the right proof gates. Its "Eight Sleep puts blood-oxygen and snoring tracking behind its top subscription tier" is a clean business-model story, and the question about whether features were "promised to existing owners" is exactly the landmine to check before pitching. A is solid, but "Beds are becoming health sensors, one mattress cover at a time" is a single-company trend costume, and it admits it needs "other examples" to stand up.
gaps_in_A: "a live clinical study with an unnamed sleep clinic" conflicts with the update's supplied fact that the study is with a named sleep clinic. If the name is missing from the brief, call it a missing asset, not an unnamed partner.

"Beds are becoming health sensors, one mattress cover at a time" stretches one product launch into a category story, then has to ask for "other examples" to prove the trend. That is a warning label, not a finished angle.

"health-equity reporter" is a little grand for a several-thousand-dollar wellness mattress feature. Subscription-economy or consumer-tech is the tighter beat; health equity needs a real affected population, not just expensive hardware.
"four viable shapes exist" overstates the set. The athlete/biohacker angle is only viable if there is a named user or usage data; otherwise it is a persona note wearing a headline.
gaps_in_B: "Why athletes and biohackers are the test market" overclaims. The update says Eight Sleep markets to them, not that they are a test market.
"the cohort most willing to pay premium prices" is invented unless Eight Sleep has buyer data. Plausible is not the same as sourced.
"heated seats by subscription, locked car features" is useful reporter context, but it is outside the supplied facts. Fine as an analogy, not as evidence unless sourced.

"journalist-fit-check" is the wrong next-step label for finding names; fit-check evaluates a known journalist. The practical next move is proof-gathering, then a fit-checked journalist list for the chosen beat.
